LETTER OF DEMAND — FINAL NOTICE BEFORE LIQUIDATION PROCEEDINGS, AND NOTICE OF THE PERSONAL LIABILITY OF DIRECTORS AND SURETIES

Dear Sirs / Madams — we act on behalf of {{client_name}}, the creditor, and are duly authorised to issue this demand. It is addressed to the company and to each of its directors. This is a formal legal demand. Please read all of it.
The company is indebted to the creditor as set out below, and the amount is due and payable in full.
WHAT HAS BEEN PAID SINCE THIS ACCOUNT WAS HANDED TO US
Still outstanding and due in full
Interest accrues on the overdue amount at 2% per month, as provided for in the agreement, until the account is paid in full.

We demand payment of {{balance}} by {{respond_by}}. A company that keeps incurring debts it has no reasonable prospect of paying may be carrying on business recklessly, which Section 22 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 prohibits. The directors should consider the company’s position with that in mind.
How the company may deal with us

items.text: Settle the account.
Payment of {{balance}} settles the account in full. A settlement figure to the intended date of payment is available on request.
Propose a payment arrangement.
Send it in writing with amounts and dates, together with the company’s latest management accounts or bank statements. Nothing is agreed until we confirm it in writing.
Dispute the debt.
If there is any dispute regarding this matter, tell us in writing with the grounds and supporting documents. We will investigate and give a written finding.

spans.text: Where any person has signed as surety and co-principal debtor for the company’s obligations, this demand is also directed at that person, and the creditor may proceed against every surety personally.

Where the National Credit Act applies to the agreement, this is also a notice in terms of Section 129(1)(a) of that Act, and the company may refer the agreement to an ADR agent, an ombud with jurisdiction or a consumer court within 10 (ten) business days of delivery.
What happens if the company does not respond
WHAT FOLLOWS IF WE DO NOT HEAR FROM THE COMPANY
If the company has not paid by {{respond_by}}, our client’s attorneys will be instructed to take the following steps:
Reported to the registered credit bureaus against the company’s registration number, where suppliers and lenders who assess the company can see it.
Our client’s attorneys serve a demand on the company in terms of Section 345 of the Companies Act 61 of 1973. If it is not paid within three weeks, the company is deemed unable to pay its debts.
An application is brought in the High Court for the company to be wound up. Control of the company and its assets passes from the directors to a liquidator.
An application is brought under Section 424 of that Act for an order declaring every director who allowed the company to trade recklessly personally liable for its debts.
Every person who signed as surety is sued in their personal capacity, and their personal assets may be attached and sold.
Reasonable legal and collection costs are claimed and added to what is owed.
The company can still avoid this. Pay, or contact {{collector_name}} on {{collector_phone}} or {{collector_email}} with a written proposal, before {{respond_by}}, quoting reference {{case_number}}.
PAYMENT MUST BE MADE INTO OUR LEGAL PRACTITIONER TRUST ACCOUNT
A payment into our trust account is verified on the day it reaches us. Do not pay any other account.
Email it to {{firm_email}} on the day you pay
Speak to {{collector_name}}, who handles this account, on {{firm_phone}}
We would prefer to resolve this matter without an application to court, and appreciate the company’s cooperation in doing so.
Note on delivery. Sent by email, with notification by SMS. Proof of sending is retained on our file.

FINAL NOTICE BEFORE CREDIT BUREAU LISTING AND LEGAL ACTION

Dear {{debtor_name}} — we act on behalf of {{client_name}}, the creditor. We sent you a notice in terms of Section 129(1)(a) of the National Credit Act, and a reminder. The period for responding has ended, and we have received no payment, no payment arrangement and no dispute from you.
WHAT HAS BEEN PAID SINCE THIS ACCOUNT WAS HANDED TO US
Still outstanding and due in full
Interest accrues on the overdue amount at 2% per month until the account is paid in full, so the amount owing grows every month this remains unresolved.
UNLESS THE ACCOUNT IS PAID OR AN ARRANGEMENT IS AGREED
If we have not heard from you by {{respond_by}}, 20 business days from the date of this notice, the following will follow.
Your default is reported to the registered credit bureaus and appears on your credit profile, where every credit provider who assesses you can see it.
One of our attorneys proceeds with legal action against you to enforce the agreement.
Summons is issued and served on you, and judgment may be granted against you for the full {{balance}}, plus interest.
A warrant of execution allows the sheriff to attach and sell your movable or immovable property, or an attachment order is granted against your salary.
Reasonable legal and collection costs are added to what you already owe.

items.text: The amount you owe grows.

Once the matter is in court, the legal costs, the sheriff’s fees and the interest are added to the {{balance}} you owe today. What you end up paying is substantially more than the amount in this notice.
A judgment goes onto your name.
It is granted for the full balance plus those costs, and it stays on record and can be enforced for many years.
The listing follows you.
It appears on your credit profile, where every credit provider who assesses you can see it, and it makes it harder to get a loan, a credit account, a vehicle or a home loan.
Paying later does not erase the listing.
The record is updated to show the account was settled, but it remains on your profile for the period the credit bureau rules allow.
Pay in full.
Payment of {{balance}} settles the account and stops every step above.
Arrange payment.
Contact {{collector_name}} and agree an amount and date. Once confirmed in writing, the listing and the handover are put on hold for as long as it is kept to.
Dispute the debt.
If there is any dispute regarding this matter that has not yet been raised with us, tell us in writing now, with the reasons.

NOTICE IN TERMS OF SECTION 129(1)(a) READ WITH SECTION 130 OF THE NATIONAL CREDIT ACT 34 OF 2005
Dear {{debtor_name}} — we act on behalf of {{client_name}}, the creditor, and are duly authorised to issue this notice. This is a formal legal notice. Please read all of it.
You are in default under your agreement with the creditor, and the full outstanding balance is due and payable.
WHAT HAS BEEN PAID SINCE THIS ACCOUNT WAS HANDED TO US
Still outstanding and due in full

Interest accrues on the overdue amount at 2% per month, the maximum rate for incidental credit agreements under the National Credit Act, and will not exceed the limits set by Section 103(5) of the Act.
What you may do — your rights under Section 129(1)(a)

The National Credit Act entitles you to refer this agreement to any of the bodies below, so that the parties may resolve any dispute or agree a plan to bring the payments up to date, at no cost to you.
Registered with the National Credit Regulator. 0860 627 627 · www.ncr.org.za
National Financial Ombud Scheme South Africa, credit division. 0860 800 900 · www.nfosa.co.za
An alternative dispute resolution agent accredited in terms of the Act, your province’s consumer court, or the National Consumer Tribunal.
If you intend to make such a referral you must do so within 10 (ten) business days of the date this notice is delivered to you.
You may also deal with us directly
You do not have to make a referral. You may resolve this matter with us on any of the following bases:

items.text: Settle the account.
Payment of {{balance}} settles the account in full. A settlement figure to your intended date of payment is available on request.
Propose a payment arrangement.
Tell us in writing what you can afford and when, with proof of income for the last three months and a breakdown of your expenses.
Dispute the debt.
If the amount is wrong, or you are not liable, tell us in writing with your reasons and supporting documents. We will give you a written finding.

spans.text: You may also bring the agreement up to date. At any time before the creditor has cancelled the agreement you may reinstate it by paying all amounts that are overdue, together with the creditor’s permitted default charges and the reasonable costs of enforcement to the date of payment.
What happens if you do not respond
WHAT FOLLOWS IF WE DO NOT HEAR FROM YOU

Once you have not responded within 10 (ten) business days of delivery, and have been in default for at least 20 (twenty) business days, the creditor may approach a court in terms of Section 130 to enforce the agreement. That may result in:
Your default is reported to the registered credit bureaus, where every credit provider who assesses you can see it.
Issued and served on you at your home or your place of work.
Granted against you for the full {{balance}}, plus interest, and recorded against your name.
A warrant of execution allows the sheriff to attach and sell your movable or immovable property.
An emoluments attachment order requires your employer to deduct before you are paid.
Reasonable legal and collection costs are added to what you already owe.

You can avoid all of this. Contact {{collector_name}} on {{collector_phone}} or {{collector_email}} before {{respond_by}}, quoting reference {{case_number}}. We would rather agree something workable with you than litigate.
